newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU farm experts fail to agree cereals penalties.
newsitem.headline: EU farm experts fail to agree cereals penalties.

text.p: European Union agriculture experts have failed to agree on a change to the system of penalties for overplanting national arable area limits, an EU official said on Wednesday.
"National experts meeting in the EU's special agriculture committee held a long discussion on Monday and Tuesday but it came to nothing," the official said.
Germany has proposed that the system of penalising farmers for overplanting base areas should be allowed to target those who are resonsible for the overshoot.
The German case is that individual Lander (states) should be penalised rather than all Lander sharing the burden of a one percent cut in EU aid for every one per cent overshoot.
"The problem is that several member states have ideas of their own which amount to letting farmers off the penalty altogether," the official said.
According to a British diplomat fears were expressed in the committtee that some changes proposed would lead to overproduction.
"This will come up again at next week's special agriculture committee and may go to the December meeting of farm ministers," the diplomat said.
